essays.stem: A villa has ordered 60 assorted sandwiches for a wedding brunch at 11:00 a.m. Describe how you would plan and prepare the order.
essays.modelAnswer: First I confirm the order: the number of guests, the time, the types of sandwich and filling, and any allergies or dietary needs, such as vegetarian or gluten-free. I check the standard recipes and work out how much bread, spread and filling I need, then check the stock and order anything missing. I write a time plan, working back from 11:00. The day before, I can cook and chill the chicken and hard-boil and chill the eggs, but I make the sandwiches as close to service as possible. On the day, I clean and sanitise the work area and set up a production line, with the bread, spread, fillings, boards and knives in order. I take out fillings in small amounts and keep the rest in the fridge. I lay out the bread in rows, spread it to the edges, fill it, top it and cut it. I make the gluten-free sandwiches first, with clean equipment. Then I cover, label and chill the platters until they are needed.
markingPoints: Confirms numbers, time, types and allergies or dietary needs
Works out quantities from standard recipes and checks stock
Writes a time plan; prepares fillings ahead and chills them
Sets up a clean production line and keeps fillings chilled
Makes special-diet sandwiches separately; covers, labels and chills

essays.stem: Explain the food safety rules you must follow when you prepare sandwiches, and why they matter.
essays.modelAnswer: Sandwiches are not cooked after they are made, so any germs that get on them are not killed. This is why hygiene matters so much. I hold a Food Handler's Permit, wear a clean uniform and hat, and wash my hands before starting and after touching raw food, bins, money or my face. I use tongs or clean disposable gloves and change the gloves when they tear or after other tasks. I wash all salad vegetables. I use separate, colour-coded boards and knives for raw food, cooked meats and salad, if the Centre uses them, so that germs do not pass between them. High-risk fillings, such as cooked chicken, ham, egg, tuna and mayonnaise mixes, are kept in the fridge at 5 °C or below, or as the Centre's food safety plan says, and taken out only in small amounts. Cooked fillings are cooled quickly before use. Finished sandwiches are covered, labelled with the date and time and chilled, and thrown away when their time is up.
markingPoints: Explains why: sandwiches are not cooked, so germs are not killed
Personal hygiene, hand washing and a Food Handler's Permit
Tongs or gloves; washed vegetables; separate boards and knives
High-risk fillings kept at 5 °C or below and taken out in small amounts
Cooked fillings cooled quickly; sandwiches covered, labelled, chilled and discarded on time

essays.stem: Describe how you would make and present a club sandwich.
essays.modelAnswer: I get my mise en place ready: three slices of white or brown sandwich bread, cooked chicken or turkey, crisp cooked bacon, lettuce, sliced tomato, mayonnaise, cocktail sticks, and a garnish and side such as crisps or a small salad. I wash my hands and use clean tongs or gloves for the fillings. I toast the three slices of bread until golden. I spread mayonnaise or butter thinly on the toast. On the first slice I place lettuce and the chicken, then add the second slice of toast, spread on both sides. On that I place the bacon, then tomato between lettuce leaves so the toast does not go soggy, and top it with the third slice, spread side down. I press it gently, put four cocktail sticks through it, one in each quarter, and cut it corner to corner into four triangles with a sharp serrated knife. I stand the triangles on the plate with the fillings facing out, and add the side and a garnish. I serve it at once.
markingPoints: Correct ingredients: three slices of toasted bread, chicken, bacon, lettuce, tomato, mayonnaise
Hygienic handling (hands, tongs or gloves)
Correct layering, with wet fillings kept off the toast
Secured with cocktail sticks and cut into four triangles with a serrated knife
Presented with fillings facing out, a side and a garnish; served at once

essays.stem: Describe four different types of sandwich and say when each would be served.
essays.modelAnswer: A closed sandwich has a filling between two slices of bread, such as ham and cheese or egg mayonnaise in hard dough bread. It is the most common type and is good for lunches, picnics and packed meals. An open sandwich has one slice of bread or toast with the topping on show, such as smoked marlin with cream cheese or ackee and saltfish. It is eaten with a knife and fork and looks attractive for lunches and buffets. Finger or tea sandwiches are small, thin sandwiches with the crusts removed, cut into strips or triangles, such as cucumber and cream cheese. They are served at afternoon tea, receptions and parties. A wrap is a filling, such as jerk chicken with lettuce, rolled up in a soft flatbread and cut in half. It travels well for picnics and beach trips. Other types are toasted sandwiches, such as a grilled cheese, served hot, the club sandwich with three slices of toast, and pinwheels for parties.
markingPoints: Closed sandwich described, with when it is served
Open sandwich described, with when it is served
Finger or tea sandwiches described, with when they are served
Wrap, toasted, club or pinwheel described, with when it is served
Uses suitable examples, including Jamaican fillings or breads

essays.stem: Describe how you would make finger sandwiches for an afternoon tea at a villa.
essays.modelAnswer: I use thin-sliced white and brown sandwich bread, and soft butter or spread at room temperature so it does not tear the bread. I prepare fillings such as cucumber with cream cheese, egg mayonnaise and ham with mustard, keeping them chilled. I slice the cucumber very thinly and pat it dry so it does not soak the bread. I wash my hands and use clean gloves or tongs. I lay out the slices in pairs, spread each slice thinly to the edges, and spread the filling evenly, not too thick. I put the top slice on and press gently. I cut off the crusts with a sharp serrated knife, using a ruler or my eye to keep it straight, then cut each sandwich into three equal fingers or four small triangles. I arrange them neatly on a platter with a doily, in rows by filling, garnish with cress or parsley, label the fillings and allergens, cover and chill until service.
markingPoints: Thin bread and soft spread; chilled fillings, cucumber dried
Hygienic handling
Spreads thinly to the edges and fills evenly
Removes crusts and cuts into even fingers or triangles with a serrated knife
Arranges neatly, garnishes, labels, covers and chills

essays.stem: Explain how you would make sandwiches safely for guests with allergies or special diets, such as a gluten-free guest, a guest allergic to egg, and a vegetarian.
essays.modelAnswer: I find out about each guest's needs when the order is taken and write them clearly on the order. I check the labels of every product, such as bread, spreads, mayonnaise, mustard and sauces, because allergens can be hidden; for example, mayonnaise contains egg, and many breads contain wheat and sometimes sesame. I make the special sandwiches first, before the others, on a cleaned and sanitised surface, with a clean board, knife and fresh spread that no other bread has touched. For the gluten-free guest I use gluten-free bread and keep it away from crumbs. For the egg allergy I use no egg filling and no mayonnaise, unless it is egg-free. For the vegetarian I use no meat or fish, for example avocado, cheese, tomato and callaloo. I wrap or plate each special sandwich separately, label it with the guest's name and what it is free from, and tell the server so that it goes to the right guest. If I am not sure about a product, I do not guess; I ask my supervisor.
markingPoints: Records each guest's need on the order
Checks product labels for hidden allergens
Makes special sandwiches first, with clean equipment and fresh spread
Correct choices for gluten-free, egg allergy and vegetarian
Wraps and labels separately, tells the server, and never guesses

essays.stem: Explain why spreads are used in sandwiches and how you would layer the fillings so that the sandwich stays fresh and is not soggy.
essays.modelAnswer: A spread, such as butter, margarine or mayonnaise, is put thinly and evenly on the bread, right to the edges. It acts as a barrier that stops moisture from the filling soaking into the bread and making it soggy. It also adds flavour and moistness, and helps hold the filling in place. Spreads should be soft enough to spread without tearing the bread. When layering, I put a dry layer next to the bread, such as a lettuce leaf, a slice of cheese or sliced meat. Wet ingredients, such as tomato, cucumber or pickles, go in the middle between dry layers, and I can pat them dry first. Moist fillings, such as tuna or egg mayonnaise, should not be too wet and are spread evenly. For sandwiches that will be kept for a while, I may pack tomato separately or leave it out. Finally, I press the sandwich gently, cover it to stop it drying out, and chill it.
markingPoints: Spread thinly and evenly to the edges
Spread is a moisture barrier, adds flavour and holds the filling
Dry layers next to the bread
Wet ingredients in the middle, patted dry; moist fillings not too wet
Covers and chills to stop drying out

essays.stem: Describe how you would present a sandwich platter for a buffet so that it looks attractive and is safe.
essays.modelAnswer: I choose a clean platter of the right size and line it with a doily or a bed of lettuce. I cut the sandwiches neatly into even shapes, such as triangles, fingers or squares, with a sharp serrated knife, so that the edges are clean. I arrange them in neat rows or a pattern, grouped by filling, with the cut side and fillings facing out so guests can see what is inside. I do not overfill the platter. I add a fresh garnish, such as parsley, cress, cherry tomatoes or sliced cucumber, for colour, without hiding the sandwiches. I place a small label for each filling, showing any allergens, such as egg, fish, milk or wheat. I cover the platter until it goes out and keep it chilled. On the buffet, I put out tongs for serving, keep the platter on ice or in a chilled display if possible, and replace it with a fresh platter rather than topping up. Sandwiches are removed when their time is up.
markingPoints: Clean platter lined with a doily or lettuce
Neat, even cuts arranged in rows or a pattern, grouped by filling
Fresh garnish for colour that does not hide the food
Labels with fillings and allergens
Covered and chilled; tongs, chilled display, replaced not topped up, removed on time

essays.stem: Explain how you would store and display sandwiches once they are made, and when they must be thrown away.
essays.modelAnswer: Once the sandwiches are made, I cover them with cling film or a lid, or wrap them, so that they do not dry out or pick up dirt. I label each tray or pack with the name of the sandwich, the date and time it was made, the use-by time and any allergens. I store them in the fridge at 5 °C or below, or as the Centre's food safety plan says, away from raw food. For display, I use a chilled display unit, or a platter set on ice, and keep it out of the sun. I check the temperature of the display during service and record it if the Centre asks. Sandwiches left out of the fridge must be thrown away after the time limit in the food safety plan, even if they look fine, and must never go back into the fridge to be served another day. I also throw away any sandwich that is past its use-by time, has been handled by a guest, or looks or smells wrong, and I record what is thrown away.
markingPoints: Covers or wraps to stop drying and keep dirt off
Labels with name, date and time, use-by and allergens
Chills at 5 °C or below, away from raw food
Chilled or iced display, out of the sun; checks temperatures
Discards after the time limit or use-by, never returns them to the fridge, and records waste

essays.stem: Describe how you would make a hot toasted sandwich, such as a jerk chicken and cheese panini, safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I check that the sandwich press or contact grill is clean, the cable and plug are not damaged, and I switch it on to heat, as the maker's instructions say. I prepare the filling: cooked jerk chicken that has been kept chilled, sliced cheese, and some sweet pepper and onion. I wash my hands and use tongs or gloves. I cut the panini roll or use thick slices of bread, and spread the outside lightly with butter or oil so that it browns. I fill it evenly, not so full that it spills out. I place it in the hot press using tongs and close the lid gently, keeping my fingers away from the hot plates. I toast it until the bread is golden and crisp and the filling is piping hot all through, with the cheese melted; I check the centre with a clean probe if the Centre asks. I lift it out with tongs, cut it in half with a serrated knife and serve it at once on a warm plate, with a garnish. Afterwards, I switch off and unplug the press and clean it when it is cool.
markingPoints: Checks and preheats the press as the maker says
Uses a chilled cooked filling; hygienic handling
Spreads the outside lightly; fills evenly
Uses tongs and keeps fingers clear; toasts until golden and hot all through
Serves at once; switches off, unplugs and cleans when cool

practical1.title: Production line: 40 finger and closed sandwiches for a villa afternoon tea
practical1.brief: Your group will make a sandwich platter for a villa afternoon tea for ten guests: 40 sandwiches in at least four fillings (for example cucumber and cream cheese, egg mayonnaise, ham and cheese, and tuna), including closed sandwiches cut into triangles and finger sandwiches with the crusts removed. One guest is gluten-free: make four gluten-free sandwiches first, with clean equipment, and plate and label them separately. Set up a production line. Each member runs one stage (laying out and spreading the bread, filling, topping and cutting, garnishing and labelling) and every member must also spread, fill and cut at least four sandwiches while the assessor watches. Present the platters with a doily, garnish and labels showing the fillings and allergens, then cover and chill them. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the area is clean.
materials: Sliced white and brown sandwich bread, and gluten-free bread
Butter or margarine, mayonnaise, cream cheese and mustard
Cucumber, eggs (hard-boiled and chilled), ham, cheese, tuna, lettuce and cress or parsley
Colour-coded boards, serrated bread knives, palette knives, tongs and disposable gloves
Platters, doilies, labels and a marker, cling film
Fridge, probe thermometer, sanitiser and cleaning cloths
photos: The production line set up, with members in clean uniform
The gluten-free sandwiches being made first, on a clean board
Bread laid out in rows and spread to the edges
Fillings being added with tongs or gloves
Crusts removed and sandwiches cut into fingers and triangles
The finished platters with doilies, garnish and labels
Platters covered and in the fridge, and the area cleaned
checklist: Washed hands, wore clean uniform with hair covered, and used tongs or gloves
Kept fillings chilled and took out only small amounts at a time
Made the gluten-free sandwiches first with clean equipment, kept them apart and labelled them
Spread thinly and evenly to the edges
Filled evenly, with wet fillings between drier layers
Cut neatly with a serrated knife, crusts removed cleanly for the finger sandwiches
Arranged, garnished and labelled the platter (fillings and allergens)
Covered and chilled the platters and cleaned and sanitised the work area
safety: Use a sharp serrated knife on a steady board; carry knives point down and never try to catch a falling knife
Keep high-risk fillings at 5 °C or below, or as the Centre's food safety plan says
Keep raw and ready-to-eat food apart, and use the Centre's colour-coded boards
Wipe spills at once and keep the floor dry

practical2.title: Hot and speciality sandwiches: club sandwich, jerk chicken panini, wraps and pinwheels
practical2.brief: Your group will prepare a lunch selection for a villa pool party: two club sandwiches (three slices of toast, cut into four triangles and held with cocktail sticks), four jerk chicken and cheese paninis or toasted sandwiches made in the sandwich press, four wraps (for example callaloo and cheese, or chicken and lettuce) cut in half on the slant, and a plate of pinwheel sandwiches. Every member must make at least one hot sandwich in the press and one cold item while the assessor watches, and every member takes part in plating and the clean-down. Cooked fillings must be chilled before use, and the hot sandwiches must be served at once, piping hot. Present each item on a suitable plate or platter with a garnish and allergen labels. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the press is switched off, unplugged and cleaned and the area is clean.
materials: Sandwich bread, panini rolls or thick-sliced hard dough bread, and soft flour tortillas
Cooked chicken (chilled), jerk seasoning, cooked bacon, cheese, callaloo, lettuce, tomato and mayonnaise
Sandwich press or contact grill, toaster, tongs and a probe thermometer
Serrated knives, colour-coded boards, palette knives, cling film and cocktail sticks
Plates, platters, garnish and allergen labels
photos: Mise en place with chilled fillings and the press checked
A club sandwich being layered on toast
The club sandwich cut into triangles with cocktail sticks
A panini in the press, lifted out with tongs
Wraps rolled and cut on the slant
All items plated with garnish and labels
The press unplugged and the area cleaned
checklist: Worked hygienically: hands washed, clean uniform, tongs or gloves
Used chilled cooked fillings and kept them cold until used
Checked the press and used it safely, with tongs and fingers clear of the hot plates
Toasted a hot sandwich until golden and piping hot all through
Layered and secured a club sandwich correctly and cut it into four triangles
Rolled a wrap or pinwheels tightly and cut them neatly
Presented the items neatly with garnish and allergen labels
Switched off and unplugged the press, and cleaned it once it was cool
safety: Check the press cable and plug before use; keep hands dry and follow the maker's instructions
Use tongs with the hot press and toaster; keep fingers away from hot plates
Use a sharp serrated knife on a steady board and carry knives point down
Keep cooked fillings at 5 °C or below until used, or as the Centre's food safety plan says
Clean the press only when it is switched off, unplugged and cool
